prompt: Which two words describe what CI has that your own computer does not?

choices.text: Clean and every
choices.why: Right: a machine with none of your local state, on every change.

choices.text: Faster and bigger
choices.why: Speed is not the point; a CI machine is often slower than a laptop.

choices.text: Remote and paid
choices.why: Where it runs and what it costs are not what makes its answer worth having.

choices.text: Automatic and silent
choices.why: CI is the opposite of silent: its result is shown on the pull request.

prompt: Put the planner's pipeline in the order it runs.
Why do the checks run on the pull request rather than after the merge?

choices.text: GitHub only allows checks on pull requests
choices.why: The planner's workflow also runs on pushes to `main`.

choices.text: After the merge the code cannot be built any more
choices.why: It can; that is what the host does with `main`.

choices.text: Tests are too slow to run on `main`
choices.why: Speed has nothing to do with where they run.

choices.text: The break stays on one branch
choices.why: Right. After the merge it is a broken main branch that everybody pulls.

prompt: `package.json` asks for `typescript` 6.0.2 and the lockfile records 6.0.3. What does `npm ci` do?

choices.text: Installs 6.0.2 and updates the lockfile
choices.why: That is `npm install`'s behaviour; `npm ci` never writes the lockfile.

choices.text: Stops with an error and installs nothing
choices.why: Right, naming both versions.

choices.text: Installs 6.0.3, as the lockfile says
choices.why: It checks that the two agree before trusting the lockfile.

choices.text: Installs both versions side by side
choices.why: Nothing is installed at all.

prompt: A colleague deletes `package-lock.json` to get past an `npm ci` error. What has changed for the project?

choices.text: Nothing; `package.json` already pins every version
choices.why: It pins the direct dependencies; the lockfile pins everything beneath them too.

choices.text: Installs get slower but stay the same
choices.why: They do not stay the same: the versions are resolved again.

choices.text: It installs that day's newest versions
choices.why: Right, which is the opposite of a pin.

choices.text: `npm ci` now works with any `package.json`
choices.why: `npm ci` refuses to run without a lockfile.

prompt: Match each behaviour to the command it belongs to.

pairs.left: Rewrites the lockfile when something changes

prompt: Why can `planner.ts` be tested without a browser?

choices.text: It takes data and returns data, with no DOM
choices.why: Right. Lesson 1 kept the page out of it for this reason.

choices.text: Vitest starts a hidden browser for every test
choices.why: Not here; these tests run in Node.

choices.text: TypeScript checks it instead of running it
choices.why: The tests run the functions; types are a separate check.

choices.text: It is compiled to `dist/` before the tests
choices.why: Vitest reads the TypeScript directly.

prompt: With the line changed to `s.date <= end`, how many minutes planned did `weekTotal` return for the week of 12 October?
Why is the test file's data four sessions at the edges of a week rather than a typical week?

choices.text: Vitest needs exactly four records
choices.why: Vitest needs nothing of the kind.

choices.text: The real data has only four sessions
choices.why: `courses.json` has six.

choices.text: Off-by-one mistakes live at the edges
choices.why: Right. The `<=` mistake changed nothing in mid-week.

choices.text: Fewer records make the tests faster
choices.why: Speed is not why; four or forty would take no time.

prompt: The `test` script is `vitest ___`, which runs once and exits instead of waiting for changes.
`src/format.ts` was never committed. On your computer, what do `npx tsc` and `npm test` say?

choices.text: Both fail on the missing import
choices.why: The file is on your disk, so nothing is missing there.

choices.text: Both pass
choices.why: Right. Only a clean copy can show this mistake.

choices.text: `tsc` passes and the tests fail
choices.why: The tests never touch `format.ts`.

choices.text: Git refuses the commit
choices.why: Git commits what you staged and warns with `??` at most.

prompt: In `git status --short`, what does `?? src/format.ts` mean?

choices.text: The file has a conflict
choices.why: Conflicts are shown with `UU`.

choices.text: The file is ignored
choices.why: Ignored files are not listed at all.

choices.text: The file was deleted
choices.why: A deletion is `D`.

choices.text: Git does not track it yet
choices.why: Right: untracked, so `commit -a` leaves it out.

prompt: Which of these mistakes would a clean checkout catch and your own computer would not?

choices.text: A test whose expected value was worked out wrong
choices.why: That fails the same everywhere.

choices.text: A package missing from `package.json`
choices.why: Right. Installed by hand, it is in your `node_modules` and in no lockfile.

choices.text: A type error in a committed file
choices.why: Your own `tsc` finds that too.

choices.text: A slow build
choices.why: A slow build is slow on both.

prompt: In the workflow, what does `on: pull_request` together with `push: branches: [main]` mean?

choices.text: It runs only when a pull request is merged
choices.why: It runs on every pull request, before any merge.

choices.text: Every pull request, and every push to `main`
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Pushes to any branch, and pull requests to `main`
choices.why: Pushes are limited to `main`.

choices.text: Only on the `main` branch, for both events
choices.why: `pull_request` has no branch filter here.

prompt: Why does each `uses:` name a forty-character commit instead of `@v7`?

choices.text: GitHub rejects tags in `uses:`
choices.why: Tags work; the problem is that they can move.

choices.text: A commit downloads faster than a tag
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: Tags move; commits do not
choices.why: Right. A moved tag would run somebody else's new code with your token.

choices.text: Version numbers are not allowed in comments
choices.why: The comment beside each one carries the version.

prompt: Which lines of the workflow limit what a compromised step could do? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: `permissions: contents: read`
choices.why: Right: the token can only read.

choices.text: `persist-credentials: false`
choices.why: Right: no token left in the clone's configuration.

choices.text: `timeout-minutes: 10`
choices.why: It limits time, not what a step may do.

choices.text: `cache: npm`
choices.why: It speeds up installs.

prompt: What does `cache: npm` keep between runs?

choices.text: `node_modules`, ready to use
choices.why: `npm ci` still builds `node_modules` from scratch.

choices.text: npm's downloads, keyed by the lockfile
choices.why: Right. It spares the network, not the install.

choices.text: The built `dist/` folder
choices.why: The build is what is being checked, so it is made fresh.

choices.text: The results of the last test run
choices.why: Tests run every time.

prompt: A pull request upgrades one dependency. What happens to the cache on its first run?
hint: What is the cache keyed by?

choices.text: The old cache is used, and the old version installed
choices.why: `npm ci` installs what the lockfile says, whatever the cache holds.

choices.text: The run fails until the cache is cleared by hand
choices.why: Nothing needs clearing; the key changes by itself.

choices.text: A new key misses, so that run downloads
choices.why: Right: one slow run, then a warm cache again.

choices.text: The cache is skipped for pull requests
choices.why: Pull requests use caches too.

prompt: CI is red on a pull request, but the Merge button still works. What is missing?

choices.text: A rule on `main` requiring the check
choices.why: Right. Without it, red is only a suggestion.

choices.text: A second job in the workflow
choices.why: More jobs do not block a merge on their own.

choices.text: `permissions: write` in the workflow
choices.why: Permissions are about the token, not merging.

choices.text: Previews turned on at the host
choices.why: Previews show the change; they do not block anything.

prompt: Each pull request was green when merged, yet `main` is broken after two merges in an hour. Which setting prevents this?

choices.text: Turning off the bypass for administrators
choices.why: Nobody bypassed anything; both were green.

choices.text: A longer `timeout-minutes`
choices.why: Time was not the problem.

choices.text: Requiring two approving reviews
choices.why: Reviewers cannot see the combination either.

choices.text: Up-to-date branches, or a merge queue
choices.why: Right. Then the check runs on what the merge will actually be.

prompt: Ten pull requests are open on a repository connected to Netlify. How many previews are there?

choices.text: One, shared, like a staging site
choices.why: That is staging; previews are per pull request.

choices.text: Ten, one per pull request
choices.why: Right, side by side.

choices.text: Eleven, counting production
choices.why: Production is not a preview.

choices.text: None until each is merged
choices.why: Previews exist before the merge; that is their point.

prompt: You want a link in a review comment to keep showing exactly what was reviewed. Which address do you paste?

choices.text: The branch address, which follows the latest push
choices.why: That one changes with every push.

choices.text: The production address
choices.why: Production does not show the pull request at all.

choices.text: The deployment's own address
choices.why: Right: one build, forever.

choices.text: Any of them, they show the same build
choices.why: They show the same build only until the next push.

prompt: `git ___ add` checks a branch out into another folder while the repository stays where it is.
In the hand-made previews, why was each branch built with its own `--base`?

choices.text: So the two builds get different hashes
choices.why: The hashes differ because the contents do.

choices.text: `host.mjs` refuses two folders without it
choices.why: It serves any folder; the paths inside the pages are the issue.

choices.text: Its links must stay inside its path
choices.why: Right. It is lesson 1's subpath, twice.

choices.text: Vite needs it to build a branch that is not checked out
choices.why: The worktree is a checkout; `--base` is about serving.

prompt: What did a host's preview give you that the hand-made one did not?

choices.text: A build of the branch
choices.why: You built both branches yourself.

choices.text: The link posted on the pull request
choices.why: Right, plus an address per preview and the clean-up.

choices.text: Two versions served at once
choices.why: `host.mjs` served both at once.

choices.text: A different stylesheet per branch
choices.why: Each build had its own already.

prompt: Which of these must not be in a preview of the planner? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Production's API key
choices.why: Right: previews get staging values.

choices.text: The branch's own `courses.json`
choices.why: That is fine; it is what the branch carries.

choices.text: A price nobody has announced yet, unless access is restricted
choices.why: Right: a preview publishes it.

choices.text: The new heading colour
choices.why: Previewing that is the point.

prompt: Why does a preview address need `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`?

choices.text: To stop people who have the link from opening it
choices.why: It does nothing to people; it speaks to search engines.

choices.text: Old versions stay out of search results
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: So the CDN does not cache it
choices.why: Caching is controlled by other headers.

choices.text: Because previews are served over plain HTTP
choices.why: Previews are HTTPS like the rest.

prompt: A pull request from a stranger's fork changes `package.json` scripts. Why is building its preview automatically a risk?

choices.text: The preview will overwrite production
choices.why: Previews never touch production's address.

choices.text: Forks cannot be built at all
choices.why: They can; the question is with what access.

choices.text: The new scripts will not be in the lockfile
choices.why: Scripts live in `package.json`; the lockfile does not list them.

choices.text: The build runs whatever those scripts say
choices.why: Right, which is why secrets are held back and some hosts ask for approval.

prompt: A pull request is green in CI, its preview looks right, and after the merge a deep link 404s in production. What did neither check cover?

choices.text: The type check, which should have caught it
choices.why: Types know nothing about how a host serves addresses.

choices.text: The host's rules for that address
choices.why: Right; lesson 4 is about those rules.

choices.text: The lockfile, which drifted after the merge
choices.why: The lockfile does not decide what a host serves at an address.

choices.text: The cache, which kept an old build
choices.why: The CI cache holds downloads, not builds.
